ICCSD teacher who drowned trying to save student to be honored at Iowa football game

In September, Hannah Jorgensen, a fifth-grade teacher at Borlaug Elementary School, died after trying to save Ahmed Osman, one of her students.
Lance Peterson, News Editor • November 23, 2026
Samantha DeFily
Iowa players lift the Heroes Trophy after a football game between Iowa and Nebraska at Memorial Stadium in Lincoln, Nebraska on Friday, Nov. 28, 2025. The Hawkeyes defeated the Cornhuskers 40-16.
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:18
Instaread

Hannah Jorgensen, an Iowa City Community School District teacher who drowned while trying to save one of her students, will be honored on Friday during the Iowa Hawkeyes Nebraska Cornhuskers football game at Kinnick Stadium. The honor is for the 16th annual Heroes Game and Jorgensen has been selected as Iowa’s Hero.

On Sept. 22, Jorgensen, a 24-year-old fifth-grade teacher at Borlaug Elementary drowned after trying to save 10-year-old Ahmed Osman who had fallen into the Coralville Reservoir after slipping on rocks during a class field trip. Osman drowned as well.

In a press release, University of Iowa athletics director Beth Goetz said the Pioneer Heroes program gives the UI the chance to honor courageous and selfless individuals.

“As an educator, Hannah dedicated her life to caring for and supporting young people, and her final act reflected that same unwavering commitment,” Goetz said in the release. “While our hearts remain with the families and community affected by this heartbreaking loss, we are honored to recognize Hannah’s remarkable life, selfless actions, and lasting impact as this year’s Iowa Hero.”

Jorgensen and Nebraska Hero Chris Preble will be honored during halftime at the game. Jorgensen’s family will attend the game to receive the honor. Both heroes will also have their names inscribed on the Heroes Game trophy.
